**Triage** — graded. Confirmed at `origin/main` `b8562ff262`, including the part that decides the route.

## The claim is false as stated

`SelectOptionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:257-280`) declares six keys, none tombstoned: `label` `:257`, `value` `:258`, `description` `:275`, `color` `:276`, **`default` `:277`** (`z.boolean().optional().describe('Is default option')`), `visibleWhen` `:278+`.

The changeset (lines 20-22) says the repeater now offers `label`, `value`, `color` and `description` — "exactly `SelectOptionSchema`'s authorable keys minus `visibleWhen`". Four offered, six declared: the difference is `{ default, visibleWhen }`. The sentence tells a reader `default` is offered. It is not.

## ⭐ The cheap window is still open — take the first route, not the second

`.changeset/object-form-option-icon-offer-withdrawn.md` is **still present on `main`**, i.e. unconsumed. So this is the one-line correction in the changeset itself, before the Version Packages PR folds it into `CHANGELOG.md` — not the after-the-fact CHANGELOG correction the card offers as its fallback.

That distinction is the whole value of grading this promptly: once the release folds it, the same fix becomes a published-changelog edit at the next version. ⛔ Do not let this sit until the window closes.

## Scope ruled

Correct the sentence in `.changeset/object-form-option-icon-offer-withdrawn.md`. Nothing else. The accurate statement is that the repeater offers four of the six declared keys, with `default` and `visibleWhen` both unoffered — and the `object.fields.options` ledger row #14327 added names both, so the changeset and the ledger should agree.

⛔ Do not "fix" this by offering `default` in the repeater. That would be a form change, it is not what the card asks, and whether the quick-add row should offer a boolean default is a separate question with its own ADR-0049 reading. This card is a text correction.

⚠️ Note for the implementer, because the two look alike: editing `.changeset/*.md` is the **sanctioned** input channel and is exactly right here. It is not the same thing as editing `content/docs/releases/`, which a code PR must never touch — release notes are compiled centrally from these changesets. Fixing the changeset is fixing the source.

## Routing

`domain:spec` — the text is `@objectstack/spec`'s own changelog entry and the accuracy question is about `SelectOptionSchema`'s declared key set. `documentation`.

`priority:p3`: no accept/reject behaviour is involved and nothing in the form or the schema moves — the card says so and it is right. It is a real card because this text ships verbatim inside the published package as what an upgrading author or agent reads to learn what the designer teaches, and it currently teaches one key wrong.

| where the sentence lives now | **`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:6702`** — `exactly \`SelectOptionSchema\`'s authorable keys minus \`visibleWhen\`, which is a …` |

⇒ A Version Packages release folded the changeset (`@objectstack/spec` is now `17.3.0`). **Triage's ruled scope is no longer executable** — the file it names does not exist. The window warning was correct and it was not met; recording that plainly rather than quietly re-scoping.

### Route ruled by this seat (the card's own stated fallback)

The card already anticipated this: *"or a CHANGELOG correction at the next version if it has already been folded."* ⇒ **Correct the sentence in place at `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`.** Everything else in triage's ruling stands unchanged and is ⛔ not reopened — in particular ⛔ **do not "fix" this by offering `default` in the repeater**: that is a form change with its own ADR-0049 reading, and this card is a text correction.

⚠️ This route is materially different from the one triage ruled, in one way that matters: it edits a **published** changelog entry rather than an unconsumed input. Two guards on that:
- it stays a **docs-only** correction of a factual error — which is the sanctioned route for a wrong release record, ⛔ never a rider on a code change;
- ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` is untouched. That surface is written centrally at release time and a code PR never edits it. `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` is the package's own changelog and is a different file.

⚠️ **One premise the dev must falsify first**: whether `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` is ever regenerated wholesale by tooling. If some generator or `check:generated` step rewrites it from inputs that no longer contain this entry, a hand edit would be reverted or would go red — in that case ⛔ stop and report rather than fighting the generator, and the card becomes a question about how this project corrects a published changelog at all.

**Closing it now, explicitly, rather than leaving the record to imply GitHub did it.** The disposition is the one PR #15454 states in its own body — *"nothing else remains to be done against it after this merges"* — and the route re-ruling that kept this card open past triage's scope is recorded in this thread and in the merged commit `c3b6da4bc`.
